The meaning: that the man or the woman testifies that "the curse of Allah" or "the wrath of Allah," i.e., by what corresponds to this sentence.

Nafi' read with the lightening of the nun of "an" in both places, and ("ghadiba Allahu") with the form of the past tense verb, and the divine name after "ghadiba" in the nominative. His reading was interpreted by taking "an" as a lightened form of the heavy one, with its operation cancelled, and its noun being a suppressed pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), elided, meaning: to magnify the matter of the fifth testimony. It was rejected by what has been established: that the predicate of the lightened "an" may not be free of one of four things: "qad," a negative particle, a particle of futurity (tanfis), or "law." What appears to me is that "an" in Nafi's reading should be taken as explanatory (tafsiriyyah), since the fifth is an oath, so it contains the sense of saying without its letters, and the explanatory form suits it.

Ya'qub recited (anna la'nata Allahi) with the (anna) lightened, the (la'natu) in the nominative, and the name of God in the genitive, like the recitation of Nafi'. He alone recited (anna ghadabu Allahi 'alayha) with the (anna) lightened, the (ghadaba) with a fatha on the dad and the ba' in the nominative, as a verbal noun (masdar), and the name of God in the genitive by annexation.

In all the recitations, the two spouses do not mention the word (anna) in the fifth oath of imprecation, for it is not found in the description of the oaths of imprecation in the books of jurisprudence or the books of Sunnah.

The wording of the fifth oath is like the wording of the four oaths. He specified for him in the supplication the particular curse, because if he is lying, he has slandered his wife and exposed her to the people's cursing and the rejection of spouses, so it was fitting that his recompense be the curse.

Al-la'nah and al-la'n: removal with contempt. It has already been mentioned in His words: ﴿And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Hijr: 35] in Surat al-Hijr.

Know that if the husband names a specific man as having committed adultery with his wife, he becomes a slanderer of that man in addition to his slander of the woman. And if he performs imprecation and completes it, the hadd punishment for slander falls from him with respect to the woman, which is clear. What remains to be considered is his slander of that man whom he attributed adultery to. The jurists differ regarding the falling of the hadd punishment for slander with respect to the man. Al-Shafi'i said: it falls from him, the hadd punishment for slander with respect to the man, because God Most High mentioned only one hadd, and because it is not established in the Sunnah that the Messenger of God ﷺ enforced the hadd for slander (qadhf) against 'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani or against Hilal ibn Umayya after the imprecation. Malik and Abu Hanifa said: the imprecation removes the hadd of the one performing imprecation for slandering his wife, but it does not remove the hadd of slander for a man he named. Their proof is that God legislated the hadd for slander.

Since these oaths entail the truthfulness of the husband's claim against the wife, it follows that the wife is regarded as an adulteress, or that her pregnancy is not from him, and so it is from fornication. Because she is under his marriage, this requires that the hadd for fornication be enforced upon her. Thus the Shari'ah does not neglect the woman's right, nor does it hold her bound by oaths whose swearer may be lying in them, since he is accused of lying to clear himself. Therefore it granted the wife the right to counter her husband's oaths, just as it granted the one testified against the right to challenge the testimony by impeachment or counter-evidence. God Most High said: ﴿And it averts from her the punishment that she testify four testimonies by God﴾, the verse. Since the wife's oaths serve to repel the husband's oaths, and the husband's oaths substitute for testimony and are called testimony, it is fitting that the wife's oaths for repelling them be called testimony too, and because they are like counter-testimony. And since they stand in the place of counter-testimony, all the wife's oaths are aimed at nullifying his claim, not at establishing her innocence or truthfulness.

Al-dar' (al-dar'): repelling with force, and it is used here metaphorically for nullification. It has been discussed at His words: ﴿And they repel evil with good﴾ [al-Ra'd: 22] in Surat al-Ra'd.

The definite article in (al-'adhab) is clearly for a previously mentioned referent, since the punishment was mentioned in His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2]. From the verse it is taken that if the woman does not swear the oaths of imprecation, the hadd is enforced upon her. This is what the reports of the hadith of imprecation in the Sunnah attest. Abu Hanifa said: if the woman refuses the oaths of imprecation, she is not subjected to the hadd, because in his view the hadd is only established by the testimony of witnesses or by confession. So, in his view, she is returned to the ruling of imprisonment, which is abrogated according to us, and in his view it was abrogated only in some cases and remained in others.

The wording of the wife's oaths is the same as the wording of the husband's oaths, exactly alike. And for her in the fifth oath is specified the supplication for the anger of God upon her if her husband is truthful, because she angered her husband by her action, so it was fitting that her recompense be the anger of her Lord upon her, just as she angered her mate.

Many branches arise from the rulings of imprecation, some of which some exegetes touch upon, and they are the subject matter of the books of furu' (positive law).

Commentary of Ibn ʿAshur (al-Taḥrir wa al-Tanwir) on Surah 24, verses 6–9 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that he is surely of the truthful.﴾ ﴿And the fifth: that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars.﴾ ﴿And it averts the punishment from her that she testify four testimonies by Allah, that he is surely of the liars.﴾ ﴿And the fifth: that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.﴾

This is a specification of the two generalities in His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ [al-Nur: 4], for among the chaste women are those who are wives of the ones who accuse them. So these, those who accuse their wives, are singled out from the ruling of His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ [al-Nur: 4], etc., since husbands alone are excused for their undertaking to speak of adultery concerning their wives when they are unable to establish it with four witnesses.

The basis of their excuse in this is the natural disposition (sajiyyah) of jealousy (al-ghayrah) that is in people's souls over their wives, and the inability to bear seeing adultery with them. So He removed from them the legal penalty for slander (hadd al-qadhf) and prescribed for them mutual imprecation (al-mulaʿanah).

In this ruling there is an acceptance of the husband's word about his wife in general, when he is careful (mutathabbitan). Indeed, after the husband's oaths, the woman is required to repel that by her own oaths; otherwise his word is accepted against her together with his oaths, and it is then equivalent to the testimony of four, and it makes her punishment obligatory if she does not repel it with her oaths.

The reason for this is that in the souls of husbands there is a restraint (wazi') that holds them back from accusing their wives of immorality falsely, and it is the restraint of shame (al-taʿyir) from that, and the restraint of love in husbands, generally. For this reason Allah named the husband's claim against her by the name of testimony, with the evident exception in His saying: ﴿And they have no witnesses except themselves﴾. And in their souls there is such jealousy over them that silence about it cannot be tolerated; in the Jahiliyyah they used to kill over it, and the man was believed in what he claimed against his wife. Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "If I found a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword, not turning the flat of it (ghayr musfih)." But jealousy may be excessive, and rivalry among men to be known for it may kindle it in souls; so Islam forbade that, since it is not the right of anyone to destroy a soul except the ruler (al-hakim). And it did not establish placing the lives of wives under the control of the differing dispositions of their husbands.

When the penalty for slander was established, the matter became difficult for husbands who come upon suspicion regarding their wives. The case of ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlani with his wife Khawlah bint ʿAsim (and it is said: bint Qays) was revealed; both were from the paternal cousins of ʿAsim ibn ʿAdi from the Ansar. Malik narrated in the Muwatta' from Sahl ibn Sa'd that "ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlani came to ʿAsim ibn ʿAdi al-Ansari and said to him: 'O ʿAsim, what do you think of a man who found another man with his wife; would he kill him, and would you kill him, or how should he act? Ask the Messenger of Allah about that for me, O ʿAsim.' So ʿAsim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and the Messenger of Allah disliked the questions and found fault with them, until what ʿAsim heard from the Messenger of Allah weighed heavily on him. When ʿAsim returned to his family, ʿUwaymir came to him and said: 'O ʿAsim, what did the Messenger of Allah say to you?' ʿAsim said to ʿUwaymir: 'You have not brought me any good; the Messenger of Allah disliked the question which I asked him about.' ʿUwaymir said: 'By Allah, I will not desist until I ask him about it.' So ʿUwaymir stood up until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the midst of the people and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds another man with his wife; would he kill him, and would you kill him, or how should he act?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Indeed it has been revealed concerning you and your companion; go and bring her.' Sahl said:
{page 163}
So they performed mutual imprecation while I was among the people at the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ presence," the hadith... So this verse became the beginning of the legislation of the ruling on husbands accusing their wives of adultery. The narrator of the story was confused by some narrators, who named him Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi. And it was added to the story: "That the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Evidence, or a penalty on your back.'" The correct view is that the occasion of revelation of the verse is the case of ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlani, and this incident occurred in Sha'ban of the ninth year after the return from the expedition of Tabuk. The verification is that they are two stories that occurred at one time or close to it.

When the Prophet ﷺ heard the words of Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah at the revelation of the earlier verse of slander, he said: "Do you marvel at Sa'd's jealousy? I am more jealous than him, and Allah is more jealous than me," meaning that it (jealousy) is not moderate in its effects, since he made among its effects that he kill whoever he finds with his wife, while Allah and His Messenger did not permit that; for Allah and His Messenger are more jealous than Sa'd. And they did not make it lawful for the husband who sees his wife committing adultery to kill the adulterer or the woman. For this reason ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlani said: "If a man finds another man with his wife, would he kill him, and would you kill him, or how should he act?"

The complement of "witnesses" (shuhada') is elided because it is evident from the context, i.e., witnesses regarding what they claimed of what they accused their wives with.

His saying "except themselves" includes what testimony cannot apply to, such as accusing with denial of a pregnancy, for which the husband had earlier claimed istibra' (the verification of the womb's cleanliness).

It is known from the hadiths on the occasion of revelation, from the reason for specifying husbands with a special ruling in the law of slander, from the wording "accuse" (yarmun), and from the mention of witnesses, that mutual imprecation is a concession (rukhsah) which Allah granted to husbands in cases of necessity, so it is not extended beyond them. For this reason Malik, in the well-known view from him and his last of two opinions, and a group, said: a couple is not made to perform mutual imprecation except when the husband claims to have seen his wife committing adultery, or denies her pregnancy with a denial based on the occurrence of the pregnancy after the certainty of the cleanliness of his wife's womb and his not having intercourse with her. If it is not like that,
{page 164}
and he accuses her of adultery, i.e., merely by hearing, or by seeing a man in the house in a situation other than adultery, or by saying to her "O adulteress" or the like of what functions as insult and abuse, then mutual imprecation is not prescribed. The husband is punished in these cases with the penalty for slander, because it is a false accusation without evidence, and there is no excuse that requires specifying it; for the excuse is the inability to bear seeing one's wife committing adultery, and the inability to bear seeing a pregnancy that is certainly not from him. Abu Hanifah, al-Shafi'i and the majority said: if he says to her "O adulteress," mutual imprecation becomes obligatory, going by their view that mutual imprecation between spouses applies to mere slander as well, holding to the unrestricted wording "accuse" (yarmun). Their analogy is weakened by the clear difference, for the jurist, between claiming adultery against a woman and insulting with words that involve attribution of adultery.

The Qur'an's naming of the oaths of mutual imprecation as "testimony" indicates that they serve to repel a claim, and the condition for legal consequences to follow from a claim is that it be established. So Malik's view is weightier than the view of the majority, for it is more penetrating to the legal reality (al-haqiqah al-shar'iyyah).

His saying: ﴿So the testimony of one of them is four testimonies, by Allah﴾ etc. Since it was impossible for husbands to dispense with testimony in such a situation, and He excused them in making such a claim, and He did not leave the matter neglected, nor did He leave women as a morsel in the mouths of those who want to defame them out of discord, excessive anger or foolishness, He imposed on husbands a testimony that is not difficult for them if they are truthful in what they claim; so He made it obligatory for them to swear by Allah four times, so that oaths stand in place of the four witnesses required for adultery in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses﴾ [al-Nur: 4] etc.

The oath was named testimony because it is a substitute for it; this is a metaphor by the relation of conceptual substitution (ʿalaqat al-hulul al-iʿtibari), and because the form of testimony is frequently used for swearing; here it was made a substitute for testimony, so it is as though the claimant brought forth from himself four witnesses by those four oaths.

The meaning of the oaths being a substitute for testimony is that they stand in its place for the excuse we mentioned just above; so they do not take all the rulings of testimony. And it should not be imagined that the oaths of mutual imprecation are accepted only from a just person (ʿadl); so if he were a transgressor (fasiq), he would not perform mutual imprecation and would not be punished with the penalty of slander; rather every
{page 165}
person whose oath is valid, his mutual imprecation is valid. This is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifah stipulated freedom, and his proof for that is linking mutual imprecation to testimony, since Allah named it testimony.

For the sake of preserving this substitution, the Imams of the four schools required that the oaths of mutual imprecation be in the formula "I bear witness by Allah" (ashhadu billah). As for what follows the formula "I bear witness", it is like an oath according to the claim he swears to, in words that admit no ambiguity.

His saying: (﴿So the testimony of one of them is four testimonies﴾) was read by the majority with the accusative on "four" (arbaʿa), as a cognate accusative (maf'ul mutlaq) of "testimony" (shahadah), so "the testimony of one of them" is with an elided predicate, indicated by the conditional sense in the relative clause and the attachment of the fa' to its predicate; the estimate is: "so the testimony of one of them is binding upon him." It is permissible that the predicate be His saying: ﴿that he is surely of the truthful﴾, by way of quoting the wording, like the saying of them: "Hijjira Abi Bakr: there is no god but Allah." Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Khalaf read "four" with the nominative, as the predicate of the subject, and the clause ﴿that he is surely of the truthful﴾ to its end is a substitute (badal) for "the testimony of one of them." There is no disagreement among the readers on the accusative of the second "four testimonies."

In His saying: ﴿that he is surely of the truthful﴾ there is a quotation of the wording of the oath, with the pronoun kept in the third-person context, i.e., he says: "Indeed I am of the truthful regarding what I claimed against her."

As for His saying: (wal-khamisah), i.e., "the fifth testimony," i.e., the one completing the number five with the four preceding it. The number noun was made feminine because it is an attribute of an elided noun indicated by His saying: (fa-shahadatu ahadihim). The estimate: "and the fifth testimony." There is no counterpart to it in the number of witnesses to adultery. So perhaps the wisdom in adding this oath to the four oaths standing in place of the four witnesses is that it reinforces the four oaths by recalling what follows from his oaths, if they were a false oath (ghamus), of being deprived of Allah's mercy, exalted is He. This is the reason it differs in its form from the forms of the four preceding testimonies. In this there is an indication that the four are those made as substitutes for the witnesses, and that this fifth is a conclusion (tadhyil) to the testimony and an intensification (taghlize) of it.

The majority read ("and the fifth: that the wrath of Allah be upon her") with the nominative, as in His saying: ("and the fifth: that the curse of Allah be upon him"), and it is a coordination of sentences (ʿatf al-jumal). Hafs on the authority of
{page 166}
ʿAsim read it with the accusative, coordinated upon the second "four testimonies," and it is a coordination of single words (ʿatf al-mufradat).

The majority read ("that the curse of Allah be upon him") and ("that the wrath of Allah be upon her") with the nun of "anna" doubled, with the verbal noun in it ("that the wrath of Allah"), and the divine name in the genitive by the annexation of "wrath" to it. On this reading it is necessary to estimate the preposition bi- entering upon "anna" in both places, attached to "the fifth," since it is an attribute of a qualified noun whose estimate is "and the fifth testimony," so that the opening of the hamzah of "anna" in both is correct. The meaning: that the man or the woman testifies that "the curse of Allah" or "the wrath of Allah," i.e., by what corresponds to this sentence.

Nafi' read with the lightening of the nun of "an" in both places, and ("ghadiba Allahu") with the form of the past tense verb, and the divine name after "ghadiba" in the nominative. His reading was interpreted by taking "an" as a lightened form of the heavy one, with its operation cancelled, and its noun being a suppressed pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), elided, meaning: to magnify the matter of the fifth testimony. It was rejected by what has been established: that the predicate of the lightened "an" may not be free of one of four things: "qad," a negative particle, a particle of futurity (tanfis), or "law." What appears to me is that "an" in Nafi's reading should be taken as explanatory (tafsiriyyah), since the fifth is an oath, so it contains the sense of saying without its letters, and the explanatory form suits it.

Ya'qub recited (anna la'nata Allahi) with the (anna) lightened, the (la'natu) in the nominative, and the name of God in the genitive, like the recitation of Nafi'. He alone recited (anna ghadabu Allahi 'alayha) with the (anna) lightened, the (ghadaba) with a fatha on the dad and the ba' in the nominative, as a verbal noun (masdar), and the name of God in the genitive by annexation.

In all the recitations, the two spouses do not mention the word (anna) in the fifth oath of imprecation, for it is not found in the description of the oaths of imprecation in the books of jurisprudence or the books of Sunnah.

The wording of the fifth oath is like the wording of the four oaths. He specified for him in the supplication the particular curse, because if he is lying, he has slandered his wife and exposed her to the people's cursing and the rejection of spouses, so it was fitting that his recompense be the curse.

Al-la'nah and al-la'n: removal with contempt. It has already been mentioned in His words: ﴿And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Hijr: 35] in Surat al-Hijr.

Know that if the husband names a specific man as having committed adultery with his wife, he becomes a slanderer of that man in addition to his slander of the woman. And if he performs imprecation and completes it, the hadd punishment for slander falls from him with respect to the woman, which is clear. What remains to be considered is his slander of that man whom he attributed adultery to. The jurists differ regarding the falling of the hadd punishment for slander with respect to the man. Al-Shafi'i said: it falls from him, the hadd punishment for slander with respect to the man, because God Most High mentioned only one hadd, and because it is not established in the Sunnah that the Messenger of God ﷺ enforced the hadd for slander (qadhf) against 'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani or against Hilal ibn Umayya after the imprecation. Malik and Abu Hanifa said: the imprecation removes the hadd of the one performing imprecation for slandering his wife, but it does not remove the hadd of slander for a man he named. Their proof is that God legislated the hadd for slander.

Since these oaths entail the truthfulness of the husband's claim against the wife, it follows that the wife is regarded as an adulteress, or that her pregnancy is not from him, and so it is from fornication. Because she is under his marriage, this requires that the hadd for fornication be enforced upon her. Thus the Shari'ah does not neglect the woman's right, nor does it hold her bound by oaths whose swearer may be lying in them, since he is accused of lying to clear himself. Therefore it granted the wife the right to counter her husband's oaths, just as it granted the one testified against the right to challenge the testimony by impeachment or counter-evidence. God Most High said: ﴿And it averts from her the punishment that she testify four testimonies by God﴾, the verse. Since the wife's oaths serve to repel the husband's oaths, and the husband's oaths substitute for testimony and are called testimony, it is fitting that the wife's oaths for repelling them be called testimony too, and because they are like counter-testimony. And since they stand in the place of counter-testimony, all the wife's oaths are aimed at nullifying his claim, not at establishing her innocence or truthfulness.

The definite article in (al-'adhab) is clearly for a previously mentioned referent, since the punishment was mentioned in His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2]. From the verse it is taken that if the woman does not swear the oaths of imprecation, the hadd is enforced upon her. This is what the reports of the hadith of imprecation in the Sunnah attest. Abu Hanifa said: if the woman refuses the oaths of imprecation, she is not subjected to the hadd, because in his view the hadd is only established by the testimony of witnesses or by confession. So, in his view, she is returned to the ruling of imprisonment, which is abrogated according to us, and in his view it was abrogated only in some cases and remained in others.

The wording of the wife's oaths is the same as the wording of the husband's oaths, exactly alike. And for her in the fifth oath is specified the supplication for the anger of God upon her if her husband is truthful, because she angered her husband by her action, so it was fitting that her recompense be the anger of her Lord upon her, just as she angered her mate.

﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that he is surely of the truthful.﴾ ﴿And the fifth: that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars.﴾ ﴿And it averts the punishment from her that she testify four testimonies by Allah, that he is surely of the liars.﴾ ﴿And the fifth: that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.﴾

Indeed, after the husband's oaths, the woman is required to repel that by her own oaths; otherwise his word is accepted against her together with his oaths, and it is then equivalent to the testimony of four, and it makes her punishment obligatory if she does not repel it with her oaths.

Ask the Messenger of Allah about that for me, O ʿAsim.' So ʿAsim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and the Messenger of Allah disliked the questions and found fault with them, until what ʿAsim heard from the Messenger of Allah weighed heavily on him. When ʿAsim returned to his family, ʿUwaymir came to him and said: 'O ʿAsim, what did the Messenger of Allah say to you?' ʿAsim said to ʿUwaymir: 'You have not brought me any good; the Messenger of Allah disliked the question which I asked him about.' ʿUwaymir said: 'By Allah, I will not desist until I ask him about it.' So ʿUwaymir stood up until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the midst of the people and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds another man with his wife; would he kill him, and would you kill him, or how should he act?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Indeed it has been revealed concerning you and your companion; go and bring her.' Sahl said:
{page 163}
So they performed mutual imprecation while I was among the people at the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ presence," the hadith... So this verse became the beginning of the legislation of the ruling on husbands accusing their wives of adultery. The narrator of the story was confused by some narrators, who named him Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi. And it was added to the story: "That the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Evidence, or a penalty on your back.'"
